The PCI‑SIG withdrew the PCIe 5.0 specification in 2023 because the industry had largely moved on to PCIe 4.0 and newer standards, leaving PCIe 5.0 with minimal adoption and a limited market demand. Consequently, the effort to maintain and promote a specification that few vendors and OEMs were actually using was deemed unnecessary, and resources were redirected toward more relevant technologies.

The PCI‑SIG decided to retire the PCIe 5.0 specification in 2023 because it had essentially been superseded by the newer PCIe 5.1 and PCIe 6.0 releases, and the industry had largely moved on to those versions. In short, the 5.0 spec was no longer needed and was being phased out to avoid confusion and duplication with the newer, more widely adopted standards.

The PCI‑SIG decided to withdraw the PCIe 5.0 specification in 2023 because the industry had not adopted it to the extent needed to justify its continued maintenance—most vendors were still using PCIe 4.0 or had already moved on to newer, more capable standards. In short, the lack of sufficient market uptake made the effort to support and evolve PCIe 5.0 untenable, so the organization chose to focus resources on the next generation of PCIe.
